name: Siansa Analysis
author: Siansa
description: For the Siansa app: each song's loudness, how it starts and ends, and its beat grids, plus similar albums and artists from AudioMuse-AI's sound analysis.

versions.changelog: A run stopped by AudioMuse-AI restarting (updating the plugin does that) no longer keeps the page on "Measuring" with its buttons off for up to 17 minutes: after 5 minutes without word from it, it counts as stopped and Measure all can be started again.
The Beat grids bar shows how far the check for where the beat stops has got, while Measure all works through the songs measured before 0.5.0. Before, it stayed full and said Ready.
Shorter texts on the settings page: each part says what it's for and how it runs in a few lines. Nothing else changes.

Measure all can now fill in where every song's beat stops. In 0.5.0 the Beat grids section counted songs measured before as done, so it offered no Measure all and its batch button was greyed out. Now it says how many songs still wait for the check, Measure all and Measure a batch now fill them in (only the beats are read again; everything measured stays in use meanwhile), and without them each song is still checked as Siansa is about to play it. Set Measure all to rounds so AudioMuse-AI's own jobs keep their turn.

Notes where a song's beat stops when it ends in a beatless outro (6 seconds or more without a beat before its dead air), so Siansa can bring the next song in after the last beat and let the outro, with its own fade, play out under it. Nothing is measured again across the library for it: new songs get it with their profile, and songs measured before are checked only when Siansa asks for them, as they're about to play, a few at a time.

Reads the tempo of drum and bass and other breakbeats right. A break repeats every beat, every one and a half and every two, and the tempo often came out at two thirds (113 BPM for 170), with the beats off the music, so Siansa never beat-matched them. Now the tempos related to the one found (double, half, one and a half, two thirds, four thirds, three quarters, and the strongest repeats) are each tried, and another is used only when its beats clearly sit better on the music; four-to-the-floor keeps its tempo. Every song's beat grids are measured again in the background, songs the app is about to play first.

Measure all goes on without a break until every song is measured (AudioMuse's own jobs wait meanwhile); rounds of 12, 10 or 5 minutes every 15 can be set instead, as before. Stop now ends any run measuring songs (Measure all, a batch now or the 15-minute task) after the song it's on. The settings page now says where the rounds are (a round running and how many it has measured, between rounds and when the next starts, waiting for one of AudioMuse's own jobs, or no round starting because the scheduled task is off) and what the last round did, and keeps itself current between rounds. Before, it stopped updating when a round ended, so the count looked stuck. A round that stopped without finishing (the worker restarted) no longer keeps the page on "Measuring" with its buttons off. The beat grids section says what 0.4.0 measures (the phrases) and why songs are read again.

Finds the phrases at each end of a song (the 4 or 8 bars it's built from: where parts come in or drop out), so Siansa's DJ radio can mix phrase on phrase, as a DJ does. The outro is read over the song's last minute. Beat grids are measured again in the background, as 0.3.0 did; the downbeat is found more surely (the kick counts double, read around the beat).

Several music servers in AudioMuse: a song is now fetched from whichever server has it, so songs only on a second or third server get their beat grids (and profiles) too. 0.3.2 put them off for a week and the run for their own server skipped them. The 15-minute task does its work once, not once per music server, so it no longer takes three times as long with three servers.

Beat grids: a song that couldn't be measured is tried again later (after an hour, 6 hours, a day, 3 days) instead of never; 0.3.1's are tried again now. Songs only on another music server are counted apart and looked at weekly. The page says why songs failed, with how many each, and has Try them all again now. Songs per run for beat grids can be any number: a round still stops when its time is up.

Beat grids have their own section on the settings page: how many songs have them and how many are still to measure, their own songs per run (0 measures them only when you ask), Measure a batch now, and Measure all with Stop. They run after the volume and fade profiles each round, in the time left over, and songs the app is about to play come first. A song that can't be read again for its beats keeps its loudness and isn't tried again every round.

Measures the beat grid at each end of every song (tempo to a fraction of a BPM, where the beats and bars fall, how beat-driven and how steady the end is), for beat-matched blends in Siansa's DJ radio. Songs measured before keep their loudness and fades and are measured again for their beats in the background.

Songs that couldn't be measured with "Not yet implemented in FFmpeg, patches welcome" are now read with the ffmpeg tool instead (the one AudioMuse-AI analyses them with), so they get loudness levelling and SmoothFade too. A packet this FFmpeg can't decode counts like a damaged one, and the error names the codec.

Similar albums and artists now work for every music server in AudioMuse (for example Emby next to Navidrome): the server the app names is looked up the way AudioMuse does it, and only albums and artists on that server are listed.
Works with several music servers: loudness profiles and similar albums and artists follow the server the app names (for example an Emby server next to Navidrome).
Siansa Analysis: volume and fade profiles for levelling and SmoothFade, and similar albums and artists from AudioMuse-AI's sound analysis.
